name: Road closure dip
description: Nine days of resurfacing on S Congress takes a bite out of the northbound approach. Real Austin rain lands inside the same window. Tickets fall about 22%, basket size holds. The owner thinks her Tuesdays are broken.
expectation: The engine should find roughly a 22% ticket shortfall over 6-14 Jul, attribute the largest share to the closure, a smaller share to the real rain days that fall inside the window, and leave a few points UNEXPLAINED - there is a hidden in-shop failure no feed carries. Basket size holding flat is the tell that this was reach, not price.
_comment_baseline: The data-generating process for the mock till. The attribution engine does NOT read this block - it estimates its own baseline from the series. Comparing the two is how we measure recovery error; see docs/DATA_FLOW.md.
_comment_events: magnitude = how big the thing was in the world (share of the 8-min polygon lost, normalised heat intensity). effect = what it did to the till, and is ground truth the engine must recover without being told.

_comment_weather: This business's sensitivity to weather, per unit of driver magnitude. The weather DRIVERS themselves are real - pulled from Open-Meteo for this parcel and scored against its own 1991-2020 normals - so the till reacts to weather Austin actually had, not weather we invented. Only the response coefficient is authored, because we have no real till to fit it from.
